description: US-28 The egg allowance. Alongside the food, DF hand every household a quantity of EGGS. Unlike food, eggs are countable — whole units, so a stated number is a number the staff member can actually hand over — and how many depends on how large the household is. DF's rule today: 8+ persons → 18 eggs, 5–7 → 12, 3–4 → 6, 1–2 → none. A PERSON IS EVERY MEMBER OF THE HOUSEHOLD ON FILE WHATEVER THEIR AGE: infants count, so two grown-ups and one baby is three persons and six eggs. Because the rule counts heads and not ages, a 13th birthday does NOT change the egg count (it still changes the counts and the price). The eggs are FREE: no charge, no effect on the price, nothing to do with the Maximalpreis, nothing written to a distribution record. THE RULE IS CONFIGURABLE like every other policy value (US-14, ADR-005): a list of rows, each a THRESHOLD (a number of persons) and the EGGS a household reaching it receives; rows added and removed; a household receives the eggs of the HIGHEST threshold it reaches; THE LIST MAY BE EMPTIED (no rows = no eggs for anyone, a legitimate setting). Refused with nothing saved when two rows name the same threshold, or when a higher threshold does not award STRICTLY MORE eggs than the one below. Staff may type rows in any order; the software sorts by threshold, checks in that order and always displays in that order. Beyond those two rules it judges nothing: an egg count need not be a multiple of six, and a threshold of one person is allowed. SHOWN on the counter, the customer record and the live household editor; NOT on the customer list and NOT on the card view (the card is designed and printed in a separate system, and the eggs are handed over at the counter). A household entitled to none shows 0, never a blank. This is the FIRST LIST-VALUED policy value, which is where most of the work is: validating a staircase, storing rows as a child table of SettingsVersion, editing rows in a form, and diffing two rules ROW BY ROW in the Änderungsverlauf. SCHEMA CHANGE: a new EggAllowanceRow model; migration history is REGENERATED, not stacked on, and the hand-written partial unique index on Customer.customerNumber must be re-added. NO new port method. DEPENDS ON BATCH 27 — it fills the tile slot the portion allowance vacated and adds a card beside the settings grid 27 re-spanned; batch 27 must be MERGED before this branch is cut. Source: tasks/prd-us-28-egg-allowance.md

userStories.title: The egg rule and the count it yields (domain)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want the number of eggs to follow from how many people are in the household under a rule that cannot hold a broken staircase, so the figure on screen is the one I hand over. Source: tasks/prd-us-28-egg-allowance.md §US-28.1 and §US-28.2
acceptanceCriteria: New PURE module src/domain/policy/eggs.ts: EggRuleRow = { readonly minPersons: number; readonly eggs: number }, EggRule = ReadonlyArray<EggRuleRow>, createEggRule(rows): EggRule and eggsFor(rule, persons): number

createEggRule SORTS by minPersons ascending and THEN validates in that order. Sorting is part of constructing the value, not something a caller does first: staff may type the rows in any order. The returned rule is always sorted and every reader may rely on it

Per-row validation runs in the INPUT order, so the index it names is the row on screen, not the row it sorts to: minPersons is an integer of at least 1; eggs is an integer of at least 0. Either failure throws InvalidSettings('eggRule.<index>.minPersons' | 'eggRule.<index>.eggs', …) through the EXISTING requireInteger helper — do NOT write a second one

Cross-row validation runs AFTER sorting: two rows naming the same minPersons throw the new DuplicateEggThreshold(minPersons); a row whose eggs is not STRICTLY GREATER than its predecessor's throws the new EggsNotIncreasing(minPersons, eggs, lowerMinPersons, lowerEggs). Checking each row against its IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR is sufficient and is what the code does — the list is sorted, so strict increase between neighbours gives strict increase throughout. Say so in a comment

Both new errors live in src/domain/errors.ts, are added to DomainErrorCode, carry the numbers that made them fail (so a German sentence can name concrete thresholds without re-deriving them), and are tiered 'refusal' in src/app/notice-tier.ts — the Record<DomainErrorCode, NoticeTier> there fails the build until both are decided, which is the mechanism working
AN EMPTY RULE IS VALID and means no eggs for anyone. There is no minimum row count and no 'at least one threshold' rule
Beyond those rules the module JUDGES NOTHING: an egg count need not be a multiple of six, a threshold of 1 person is allowed, and a row awarding 0 eggs is allowed
eggsFor(rule, persons) returns the eggs of the HIGHEST threshold that persons reaches, and 0 when it reaches none

eggsFor takes an already-validated EggRule, so it does NO sorting and NO checking of its own — the type IS the invariant, which is why createEggRule is the only way to make one. The doc comment says so, so the next reader does not add a defensive re-sort
The doc comment on eggsFor states that the rule counts HEADS AND NOT AGES, and why the eggs are therefore untouched by a 13th birthday
STRICT TDD, the invariant-breaking test written FIRST, one named test per rule, named after the rule rather than the function

createEggRule named tests: 'accepts DF's own rule'; 'accepts an empty rule'; 'accepts a single row'; 'sorts rows typed out of order'; 'refuses two rows naming the same threshold'; 'refuses a higher threshold awarding the same eggs'; 'refuses a higher threshold awarding fewer eggs'; 'refuses a threshold below one person'; 'refuses a fractional threshold'; 'refuses a negative egg count'; 'refuses a fractional egg count'; 'accepts an egg count that is not a multiple of six'; 'accepts a threshold of one person'; 'names the typed row, not the sorted row, when a value is malformed'

eggsFor named tests, against DF's rule (3→6, 5→12, 8→18): 'awards nothing to a household below every threshold' (1 and 2 persons); BOUNDARY 'awards six from three persons'; 'awards six at four persons'; BOUNDARY 'awards twelve from five persons'; 'awards twelve at seven persons'; BOUNDARY 'awards eighteen from eight persons'; 'awards eighteen to a very large household' (20 persons — there is no upper row and the top one keeps applying); 'awards nothing under an empty rule'; 'awards nothing to a household of nobody'
The module is PURE: no I/O, no clock, no import from Next.js, React or Prisma. src/architecture.test.ts and the fd/domain-boundary ESLint rule still pass
Domain coverage stays at 100% — every refusal branch above has a named test: npm run test:coverage
